D012-D021_h001.question: It’s gotten to the point where just looking at food can send me spiraling. I get this awful tightening in my chest, my heart races, and I just *know* it will make me big. It’s been building for about eight months now. I’m so afraid of putting on weight that I’ve started avoiding everything, especially anything that even looks like it might have a lot of calories. I used to love cooking as a kitchen porter, but now, being around all that food, it's torture. My daughter, bless her heart, tries to get me to eat, but I just can't. The thought of ingesting something that will make me gain weight fills me with dread. It’s not that I’m afraid of choking, or getting sick, or any of that, it’s just the weight. I’ve lost so much, and I still feel like I need to lose more. I tell myself it’s for my health, you know, being a widow and on my own now, but honestly, it’s about being thin.
D012-D021_h001.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D012-D021_h002.question:
"Honestly, doctor, it's become debilitating. For the past year, I've just been terrified of food. Not all food, mind you, but anything that feels... heavy, or like it could make me gain even an ounce. I used to love designing kitchens, but now even looking at some ingredients on Pinterest sends my heart racing. I'll start sweating and get so short of breath, like I can't catch it. It’s particularly bad around anything remotely rich or fatty; I envision myself gaining weight instantly.

My husband tries to be understanding, but he doesn't get how much distress thinking about those things causes me. It’s not just the food itself that scares me, like I’m afraid of choking or getting sick. It's really about the weight. The thought of stepping on the scale after eating something "bad" just fills me with dread; my hands will tremble, and I just can't shake the anxiety. It's been constant for the past year; I'm exhausted."
D012-D021_h002.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D012-D021_h003.question:
"Well, doctor, lately it's gotten pretty bad. I’m a truck driver, on the road constantly, and it used to be I loved those big open stretches. Now, though, just thinking about a long drive, especially if there’s a chance of rain or rough weather, my stomach just knots up. I get all shaky and can barely concentrate on anything else. It’s a gnawing feeling, like dread, and it’s always about the worst-case scenario.

But it’s not just that. The real problem, and what’s got me here, is how I’ve been with food. My wife, bless her heart, tries to make my favorite meals, but I can barely look at most of it. I’ve started avoiding certain foods altogether because I’m absolutely terrified of putting on weight. I analyze everything on the plate, thinking about what it’ll do to my body. It feels like a constant war, and I just can’t seem to win."
D012-D021_h003.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D012-D021_h004.question: "It started subtle, but now it's taken over. I drive a subway, and even underground, I feel like I'm constantly on edge. I used to enjoy my food, but lately, just thinking about certain things, especially anything fatty or sugary, makes my stomach clench. It's not a fear of *the food itself*, not like I'm worried about choking or getting sick. It's more... the fear of what it will *do to me*. The thought of gaining weight, even a pound, fills me with dread. It’s like a paralysis; I’ll freeze up, unable to eat when everyone else is, making excuses. Sometimes, the anxiety around it is so intense, it’s like a physical threat, like encountering a giant spider. Even the smell of certain foods can make me just shut down. This has been going on for over six months now, and my wife is really worried."
D012-D021_h004.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D012-D021_h005.question: "Lately, I've just felt sick to my stomach about eating. It started subtly, maybe around six months ago, but it's really gotten out of hand. I’m a long-haul driver, divorced, so I’m used to grabbing quick meals, but now, the thought of certain foods—anything greasy, really, or even just a full plate—sends a shiver down my spine. It’s not that I'm worried about choking, or that I’ll throw up, it's that those types of foods, or even just too much food, will make me gain weight. I’ve always tried to stay fit for the road, but this is different. I’ll look at a burger, and my mind just races with how many calories it has, and how much bigger I’ll get if I eat it. It's actually a similar feeling to when I'm driving through a huge thunderstorm; that fear and dread of losing control. I end up just skipping meals, or eating something tiny, like a single piece of fruit, just to avoid that feeling of getting bigger."
D012-D021_h005.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Specific Phobia
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D012-D021_h006.question: "Well, doctor, it's gotten to the point where I dread meal times. I used to enjoy cooking, but now the thought of food, especially certain things, just sends me into a panic. It’s not that I'm afraid of choking, or that I think I'll get sick from the food itself. It’s more… if I eat it, I just know it’ll go straight to my hips. The fear of seeing an extra pound or two on the scale is overwhelming. I’ve started bringing my little prayer beads with me to the dinner table, just to get through it if my daughter insists I eat. Even then, the anxiety is immediate, a real rush that makes my heart pound. I avoid so many foods now, not because I'm scared of the food, but because of what it might do to my weight. It's truly become such a struggle just to live a normal life."
D012-D021_h006.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D012-D021_h007.question:
I'm here because things have gotten out of hand. For months now, I've had this intense fear about certain foods, especially anything new or unfamiliar. Even thinking about trying something I haven't vetted sends shivers down my spine. I teach math, so I'm used to order and predictability, but this… I'll admit, it's gotten pretty severe, I'm almost paralyzed, and it's getting harder to move on with my daily activities when I have to think about food.

The thing is, it’s not really about the food itself, you know? It’s what it *does* to me. If I eat something that isn't on my approved list, I'm terrified of gaining weight. That's the real fear. Sometimes, I’ll prepare new food, but I won’t touch it unless my colleague is there to "supervise" me, and even then, I barely endure it. My students are starting to notice I skip lunch. I just can’t risk seeing the scale go up. It’s been going on for seven or eight months now, and it's exhausting.
D012-D021_h007.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D012-D021_h008.question:
"It all started subtly, a little over a year ago. I've always been pretty meticulous, which helps with teaching, but this has gotten out of control. I've become terrified of certain foods, especially anything with even a little bit of fat or sugar. It's not that I'm afraid of *choking* on them, or *vomiting* -- no, that's not it at all. It's the thought of what they'll *do* to my body. The idea of eating a cookie or anything fried sends shivers down my spine because I just know it will make me gain weight. My husband tries to get me to eat, but I can't. I'll make elaborate excuses to avoid family dinners, or make myself a tiny, bland meal that I know won't add any extra pounds.

And it's not just food. I've always had a huge fear of spiders, ever since I was a little girl. If I see one, even a tiny one, I freeze up and feel this overwhelming panic. I'll immediately leave the room, or even the house if I have to. I've even changed my route to school to avoid a house I know has a spider web on the porch. I absolutely cannot be around them."
D012-D021_h008.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D012-D021_h009.question: "Lately, I've just been terrified of eating. It’s not that I'm worried about choking, or that I’ll throw up, or anything like that, like those times when I was a kid and certain textures made me gag. No, this is different. Every time I even think about putting food in my mouth, especially anything significant, I get this overwhelming panic. My heart starts racing, palms sweat, and I just freeze. It’s an immediate, visceral reaction. I try to push through it, especially at home with my wife; I don't want her to worry. I’ll sit at the dinner table and just pick at my plate, forcing myself to endure it, but internally, I'm a wreck, consumed by this intense anxiety. This has been going on for the past six months, and I've lost a significant amount of weight. It’s hard to admit, but deep down, **the fear driving all of this, the reason I'm so scared of food, is because I'm terrified of gaining weight.** I know it sounds irrational, especially with my job, where I need to be strong, but I can't shake it."
D012-D021_h009.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D012-D021_h010.question: "I've been dealing with this for about eight months now, and it's just getting worse. It started with certain foods, but now it's almost everything. I feel this intense dread, this panic really, if I even think about eating something that might make me gain weight. It's not about choking or getting sick; it’s always about the fear of gaining weight, of getting fat. If I'm forced to eat, I can barely do it, and only if my friend is there or if I have a specific, safe food that I’ve meticulously portioned out. Even then, it’s a terrifying ordeal sometimes. I analyze everything on the label, every calorie, every gram. It’s exhausting, and it’s taken over my life."
D012-D021_h010.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D012-D021_h011.question:
It's been close to a year now, maybe a little more, since I first started feeling this way. I’ve always been particular about what I eat, but lately, it’s gone way beyond that. I dread meal times, and any new food, especially if it’s outside my very limited safe list, sends my anxiety through the roof. I feel like I have to force myself to just be in the same room as certain dishes, and it's absolutely exhausting holding it together.

The real problem is, all of this food avoidance, it’s not really about the food itself. It’s about my weight. I’m utterly terrified of gaining even a single pound. If I eat something I consider “bad,” I feel an overwhelming panic, convinced I’ll balloon up overnight. Even though everyone, especially my wife, tells me I'm too thin, I just see myself as needing to be smaller. I've become obsessed with how my body looks in the mirror, always finding something wrong, always feeling like I need to lose more. I know it sounds irrational, but the idea of being heavy... it's a constant, crushing fear that dictates everything I put in my mouth.
D012-D021_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D021_h012.question:
(Patient's subjective description):

"I really don't know what's happening to me. It started about eight months ago, I think, when I looked at myself in the mirror and realized how much weight I'd gained. All of a sudden, I just couldn't bring myself to eat like I used to. I’ve always been particular about what goes into my baked goods, making sure everything is just right, but now it's translated to my own plate in a really unhealthy way. I even find myself dreading the thought of certain foods—anything high in calories, really. It’s not that I’m afraid of choking on it; it’s more about what it’ll do to my body, about putting on even a tiny bit of weight.

To make things worse, if I have to go to the doctor for anything, even a vaccination, my heart races. I get so scared of seeing the needle or even just the sight of blood. My daughter usually has to come with me, and I cling to her hand like I’m a child, just to get through it. It’s embarrassing at my age. It feels like my body is just… betraying me."
D012-D021_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D021_h013.question: "Well, doctor, it's gotten to the point where I dread meal times here in the home. It’s not the food itself, you understand. My appetite is still good enough, but I just can't bring myself to eat much of anything they put in front of me these days. It’s been happening for a few months now. I worry constantly about putting on weight. I look at the portions, and all I can think about is becoming stout, especially at my age. I pick at my food, trying to make it last, but end up leaving most of it. I even started cutting out certain textures, and things like bread—anything starchy makes me nervous. I've heard some of the younger residents talk about spiders, how they make you jump, but for me, it's more about how much food is on my plate and what it might do to my figure. I find myself making excuses not to go to the dining room sometimes, or I'll go late so I can avoid most of the meal."
D012-D021_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D012-D021_h014.question: "Lately, food feels like my biggest enemy. I avoid anything that remotely seems unhealthy, constantly checking labels and portion sizes. D012-D021_h015.question: "It all started subtly, I guess, about seven months ago. I remember seeing a patient aspirate during my shift, and it just… stuck with me. Now, every single meal is a battle. I'm terrified of choking, absolutely petrified. I know it sounds irrational, especially me being a nurse, but the thought of a speck of food going down the wrong way, of that feeling of not being able to breathe... it just paralyzes me. I try to chew endlessly, or cut things into tiny pieces until they're nearly liquid. It’s exhausting. I avoid certain textures, anything I perceive as a choking hazard. I’m always hungry, but the fear of gaining weight if I eat 'unsafe' foods and the overwhelming anxiety of choking have me stuck. I can't just avoid it; I have to eat something, and each time I force myself to, my heart races and I feel like I'm suffocating just thinking about it going down."

A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
